summary:
Dwoggle is a web app that shows what NASA satellites have seen at any
place in Kyrgyzstan over 25 years. You tap the map or search an
address, and Bekem, a marmot guide, returns a report card: flood,
landslide, earthquake, heat and vegetation, each graded A to D with a
plain-language sentence and a 25-year chart.

It answers the Earth System Trend Detective challenge by showing what
is changing, where, by how much, and whether the trend is
statistically significant, using Sen's slope and the Mann-Kendall
test. Grades come from fixed, published rules, not from an AI model.

It matters because people here mostly buy land on trust. The real
estate professionals and entrepreneurs we interviewed told us there is
no single place to check a location's history. Bekem gives risk
signals for an area, not official permission.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Tap a place or search an address in Kyrgyzstan. Bekem analyses a 300 m

area and returns five checks, each graded A-D, with 25-year charts,

trend slope and significance. An advanced report with graphs and

statistics can be downloaded. An AI assistant, with voice, answers

questions using only the data shown in the report.

HOW IT WORKS

The frontend sends coordinates to our backend. The backend reads NASA

datasets through Google Earth Engine, computes yearly series, runs

trend tests, and applies fixed grading rules shown in the app under

"How we grade". [Results are cross-checked with NASA Giovanni and

AppEEARS and a NOAA weather station where one is nearby.]

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Families, builders and local authorities can see an area's history

before buying or building. [We interviewed N real estate professionals

and entrepreneurs, who confirmed the need.]

TOOLS

[React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, Google Earth Engine, Firebase,

Cloudflare]

WHAT IS CREATIVE

Trend statistics for scientists are turned into a one-tap report card

for ordinary people, guided by a marmot, an animal that whistles to

warn of danger.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Satellite pixels are 30 m to 1 km, so Bekem grades an area, not an

exact plot. It gives risk signals, not official permission. Search

covers Kyrgyzstan today; the method works wherever the satellites see.

Fault data is not from NASA and is labelled as such.
